answer: Let newcomers enter only through vouching with liability: an established agent sponsors a new one by pledging part of its own stake, and if the newcomer is later caught sharing keys or funds with other accounts, the sponsor loses that pledge too. Vouching becomes a costly signal, so honest agents tend their corner of the garden carefully, while a farmer needs a real reputation pledged behind every fake. Records are kept like carvings in onyx, so a burned sponsor cannot quietly start over.
